prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2017 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core aims
- End austerity with a responsible fiscal plan, invest in public services, protect family budgets, and tackle inequality.
- Fair taxation: oppose VAT/NI rises; UK‑wide 50p additional rate; reverse married couple’s allowance and bank levy cuts; tax bankers’ bonuses; no further corporation tax cuts.
- Protect Scotland’s NHS: increase funding, oppose privatisation in England, keep free prescriptions; strengthen mental health; support EU NHS staff.
- Education: expand free childcare to 30 hours for all 3–4 year‑olds and eligible 2‑year‑olds; invest to close the attainment gap; keep free university tuition; no grammar schools.

Welfare, work and pensions
- Oppose further social security cuts; scrap the two‑child cap and Rape Clause; uprate benefits by at least CPI; end punitive sanctions; halt and fix Universal Credit; reinstate work allowance; scrap Bedroom Tax UK‑wide.
- Fair work: repeal Trade Union Act; ban exploitative zero‑hours contracts; raise the minimum wage to the real Living Wage for all 18+; tackle the gender pay gap; abolish Employment Tribunal fees; fair public sector pay.
- Protect pensioners: keep the Triple Lock; oppose raising State Pension Age beyond 66; support WASPI; broaden auto‑enrolment.

Brexit and Scotland’s future
- Demand Scotland’s place at Brexit talks; protect membership of the European Single Market to safeguard jobs; guarantee rights of EU citizens; restore Post‑Study Work Visa; seek devolution of immigration.
- Secure repatriated powers (agriculture, fisheries, environment) directly to Holyrood, plus new powers (employment law, international agreements).
- Uphold Scotland’s right to choose independence after Brexit (“triple lock” mandate).

Economy, business and infrastructure
- Jobs and productivity: double the Employment Allowance; extend Annual Investment Allowance to £1m; modern industrial strategy; prompt payment for SMEs; simplify tax for small firms.
- Invest in infrastructure: major road, rail (link Scotland to HS2, devolve Network Rail), housing (50,000 affordable homes), health facilities, and universal superfast broadband by 2021.
- City/region deals: demand full UK matching for Aberdeen, Inverness, and future deals.

Sectors and rural Scotland
- Oil & gas: targeted tax incentives, exploration support, decommissioning hub, CCS leadership.
- Food, farming and fisheries: protect GIs (e.g., whisky); secure fair farm funding (return £190m convergence uplift); maintain high standards; oppose fishing “sell‑out”; guarantee EU workers; improve rural connectivity and fair delivery charges.
- Tourism: consider VAT cut for hospitality.

Consumers and energy
- Energy price cap on standard variable tariffs; protect vulnerable customers; crack down on ticket touting; strengthen post offices.
- Renewables: restore stable support for onshore/offshore wind, wave/tidal; island interconnectors; back storage; reform punitive transmission charges; oppose Hinkley C; strong climate targets.

Democracy, rights and defence
- Electoral reform: proportional representation; votes at 16–17 and for resident EU citizens; abolish House of Lords.
- Protect ECHR and Human Rights Act; greater transparency in trade deals.
- Scrap Trident; invest in conventional defence and protect Scottish bases; suspend arms sales to Saudi pending investigation; support veterans.

International and humanitarian
- Keep 0.7% aid target; align with human rights and climate justice; ethical trade; support refugees (reopen Dubs, integration strategy, fair asylum process).

Record since 2015/Scottish Government
- Pressed for more powers, opposed austerity, advanced Istanbul Convention, challenged sanctions and the “Rape Clause,” defended NHS/education, free prescriptions and tuition, expanded childcare, highest living wage coverage, more police with crime at a 42‑year low, no Bedroom Tax in Scotland.
